migration_summary: Blocking btree index build on a continuously written hot visibility table; exclusive locks plus query killers abort the build under production write load.
migration_sql: CREATE INDEX by_root_workflow_id ON executions_visibility (namespace_id, root_workflow_id, (COALESCE(close_time, '9999-12-31 23:59:59')) DESC, start_time DESC, run_id);
schema_summary: executions_visibility hot table on busy Temporal clusters (~120GB visibility DB, tens of millions of rows).

risk_flags.message: Non-concurrent CREATE INDEX on a continuously written visibility table can block writes and trip query killers.

risk_narrative: Standard CREATE INDEX holds write locks while building on a table that receives constant visibility traffic. On production-scale Temporal (~1TB persistence / ~120GB visibility), schema updates during deploy repeatedly failed when deadlock detection terminated long-blocking DDL.
lessons_learned: On high-traffic tables prefer CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside explicit transactions. Expect much longer build time on large tables; plan maintenance windows or online index builds.
surprise_notes: Index DDL that succeeds in staging can fail in production solely due to write volume and lock timeouts—not because the SQL is invalid.

documented_outcomes.error_message: Production deploy schema updates failed: blocking CREATE INDEX on busy executions_visibility (GitHub issue #6273).

prediction_summary.risk_explanation: Underestimated lock contention on always-on visibility traffic.
